question: The potential difference across a copper wire is 5.0 V when a current of 0.5 A flows through it. The resistance of the wire is:
solution:
The correct answer is__** 10.0 Ω.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula for calculating resistance is **R = V/I, **where V is the potential difference and I is the current flowing through the wire.
 
• Plugging in the given values, R = 5.0 V / 0.5 A = **10.0 Ω.**
 
• Therefore, the **correct answer **is 10.0 Ω.
 
• Copper wire is a** good conductor of electricity** due to its **high **electrical conductivity and** low** resistivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The difference in** charge carrier energy** between two places in a circuit is known as the** potential difference.**
 
• The ease with which an **electric current** can pass through a material is measured by its **electrical conductivity.**
 
• The amount of **obstruction **to current passage in an electrical circuit is measured as** resistance**.
